items.stem: What is the central promise of an ERP system?

options.text: Integrated processes and data sharing a single source of truth
options.rationale: Correct: ERP integrates functions around one consistent data model.

options.text: A faster version of standalone accounting software
options.rationale: ERP is defined by integration across functions, not just accounting speed.

options.text: A tool that eliminates the need for any business process
options.rationale: ERP supports processes; it does not remove them.
That is the opposite of ERP's integrated model.

items.explanation: Correct: ERP integrates functions around one consistent data model.

items.stem: Which statements about ERP implementation are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Heavy customisation increases cost and upgrade difficulty
options.rationale: Correct: customisation raises long-term maintenance and upgrade burden.

options.text: Configuring the system to fit standard processes is usually preferable
options.rationale: Correct: configuration keeps the system maintainable and upgradable.

options.text: Customising to preserve every old process is best practice
options.rationale: This entrenches legacy inefficiencies and raises cost.

options.text: Training and change management are unnecessary
options.rationale: Adoption depends heavily on training and change management.

items.explanation: Correct: customisation raises long-term maintenance and upgrade burden.
